# Light Settings (Cycles) [¶](https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/5.2/render/cycles/light_settings.html\#light-settings-cycles "Link to this heading")

Reference

Panel:

Properties ‣ Object Data
and Shader Editor ‣ Sidebar ‣ Options

Next to lighting from the background and any object with an emission shader,
lights are another way to add light into the scene.
The difference is that they are not directly visible in the rendered image,
and can be more easily managed as objects of their own type.

## Light [¶](https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/5.2/render/cycles/light_settings.html\#light "Link to this heading")

[Light settings](https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/5.2/render/lights/light_object.html) for all renderers.

### Beam Shape [¶](https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/5.2/render/cycles/light_settings.html\#beam-shape "Link to this heading")

Spread Area Lights

How wide the emitted light fans out controlling how diffused the area light is.
Larger values create soft shadows while smaller values create sharper light
simulating a [gridded softbox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Softbox).

![../../_images/render_lights_light-object-area-spread.png](https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/5.2/_images/render_lights_light-object-area-spread.png)

Example of Spread at different angles. [¶](https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/5.2/render/cycles/light_settings.html#id2 "Link to this image")

## Settings [¶](https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/5.2/render/cycles/light_settings.html\#settings "Link to this heading")

Max Bounces

Maximum number of times light from the light is allowed to [Bounce](https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/5.2/glossary/index.html#term-Light-Bounces).
Limited by [scene-wide bounce settings](https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/5.2/render/cycles/render_settings/light_paths.html#bpy-types-cyclesrendersettings-max-bounces).

Cast Shadow

By disabling this option, light from lights will not be blocked by objects in between.
This can speed up rendering by not having to trace rays to the light source.

Multiple Importance Sample

By default lights use only direct light sampling. For area lights and sharp glossy reflections, however,
this can be noisy,
and enabling this option will enable indirect light sampling to be used in addition to reduce noise.

Shadow Caustics

Mark a light as a refractive caustic caster. This setting can be used in conjunction with the
[Cast and Receive caustics object settings](https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/5.2/render/cycles/object_settings/object_data.html#bpy-types-cyclesobjectsettings-is-caustics-caster)
to selectively speed up refractive caustic rendering of select objects.

Portals Area Lights

Area lights can also function as light portals to help sample the environment light,
and significantly reduce noise in interior scenes.
Note that rendering with portals is usually slower, but as it converges more quickly, less samples are required.

Light portals work by enabling the _Portal_ option, and placing areas lights in
windows, door openings, and any place where light will enter the interior.

In outdoor scenes most rays do not bounce much and just fly off into the sky and therefore,
light portals are not helpful for outdoor scenes.

![../../_images/render_cycles_light-settings_portals2.jpg](https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/5.2/_images/render_cycles_light-settings_portals2.jpg)![../../_images/render_cycles_light-settings_portals.jpg](https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/5.2/_images/render_cycles_light-settings_portals.jpg)

White Room model by Jay Hardy. [¶](https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/5.2/render/cycles/light_settings.html#id3 "Link to this image")

## Nodes [¶](https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/5.2/render/cycles/light_settings.html\#nodes "Link to this heading")

In Cycles, lights can be fully defined using shader nodes.
This allows creating complex, physically based light behavior that goes beyond
the basic light settings.

Note

The basic [Light settings](https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/5.2/render/lights/light_object.html)
are applied on top of the light output node.

Light shader nodes are edited in the [Shader Editor](https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/5.2/render/shader_nodes/index.html)
when the editor is set to _Light_ context and a light object is selected.

### Emission Shader [¶](https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/5.2/render/cycles/light_settings.html\#emission-shader "Link to this heading")

Light objects use an [Emission](https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/5.2/render/shader_nodes/shader/emission.html) shader
to define their output.

The _Emission_ shader controls:

- **Color**: The spectral color of the emitted light.

- **Strength**: The intensity of the emitted light.


The output of the _Emission_ shader must be connected to the
[Light Output](https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/5.2/render/shader_nodes/output/light.html) node.

### Using Shader Nodes [¶](https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/5.2/render/cycles/light_settings.html\#using-shader-nodes "Link to this heading")

By default, lights use a simple node setup consisting of an _Emission_ shader
connected directly to the _Light Output_.

More advanced setups can be created using additional shader and utility nodes, for example:

- Mixing multiple _Emission_ shaders to create layered light colors.

- Using [Texture](https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/5.2/render/shader_nodes/textures/index.html) nodes to vary light color
or intensity across the light surface.

- Driving light intensity or color using math nodes or animation.


This makes it possible to create effects such as patterned lights, animated flicker,
or lights that change color based on time or other inputs.

### Light Output [¶](https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/5.2/render/cycles/light_settings.html\#light-output "Link to this heading")

The [Light Output](https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/5.2/render/shader_nodes/output/light.html) node defines the final
shader used by the light object.
Only shader nodes connected to this output affect the light’s appearance in Cycles.

### Limitations [¶](https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/5.2/render/cycles/light_settings.html\#limitations "Link to this heading")

- Shader-based light definitions are only supported in **Cycles**.
EEVEE uses simplified light models and ignores light shader node trees.

- Only _Emission_-based shading contributes to lighting.
Other shader types (such as _BSDF_ shaders) have no effect when used on lights.


Using shader nodes for lights provides fine-grained control and enables procedural
lighting workflows that are not possible with standard light settings alone.",
